question: According to the census of India 2011, which group of states and union territories from the following recorded the highest literacy rate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala and Lakshadweep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate in India according to the 2011 census, with a literacy rate of 93.91%.
 
• Lakshadweep followed closely with a literacy rate of 92.28%, making it one of the top regions with high literacy rates.
 
• The high literacy rate in Kerala is attributed to its long-standing emphasis on education and the effective implementation of various educational schemes.
 
• Lakshadweep's high literacy rate can be credited to the concerted efforts by the administration to improve educational infrastructure and access to education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India**

 
 
• The Census of India is a decennial exercise conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The first complete census was conducted in 1881, and it has been carried out every 10 years since then.
 
• The primary objective of the census is to collect demographic data to help in planning and policy-making for the country's development.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• Literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people who are able to read and write with understanding at a specified age.
 
• In India, the literacy rate is calculated for individuals aged seven years and above.
 
• A high literacy rate is an indicator of the effective implementation of educational policies and a well-established educational infrastructure.
 
• It is crucial for the socio-economic development of a region as it impacts employment, health, and overall quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Educational Policies in Kerala**
 
 
• Kerala has a long history of progressive educational policies and has made significant investments in education.
 
• Initiatives such as the universalization of elementary education, the mid-day meal scheme, and the encouragement of public-private partnerships have been pivotal.
 
• The state has consistently focused on improving the quality of education and ensuring access to education for all sections of society.
 
• Kerala's high literacy rate is often cited as a model for other states in India to emulate.
